mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the previous month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous three months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous two months signals increased economic activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST increases by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals an easing monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods with a sustained decrease in FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over the previous month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a robust labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous two months signals a slowdown in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% over the previous two months and GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% annualized, it signals strong economic demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% and GDPC1 annualized growth > 2% in 2 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increase by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous two months signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5pp.
